After completing Chained Echoes and getting all the achievements, I consider this one of the best turn-based RPGs I've ever played. The combat is interesting and stays challenging up until the end, there is plenty to explore and hidden secrets to uncover, and the story is well-written and at times emotionally moving. I'm really impressed with this game, you can tell the developers made it with a lot of heart. 

The only aspect I would change is the crystal system, because it gets cumbersome when you have dozens of crystals that you want to sort through and manually combine. You can use auto-combine, but it's not the same. I also would've appreciated an endgame crystal merchant to make collection simpler. Thankfully, you don't necessarily need to dive deep into the crystal system, except maybe in the endgame stage.

This wasn't a game, it was a journey. It was a great one from its graphics to QOL to story. EXTREMELY UNDERRATED. If you feel like playing a JRPG you should for sure play Chained Echoes. Everything is perfect, though the story might feel grand and some part of it might not make sense sometimes and there were some parts I weird about, that being said there were also great plot twists and the characters felt so alive(well at least for me). Overall this is a great game id love to recc! 8.8/10

Chained Echoes is the kind of game that feels like it came straight out of my dreams: a 90s-style pixel-art JRPG that pays homage to genre classics such as Final Fantasy VI, Chrono Trigger, Suikoden, and many others.

Developed by a single developer over roughly seven years, Chained Echoes is the quintessential Japanese-style RPG—a genuine love letter to the genre.

What the developer understood perfectly is the difference between honoring the past and preserving its ashes. Many of the most tedious and grindy mechanics of classic JRPGs are simply not here. Progression is closely tied to completing quests and defeating bosses, so forget about spending hours grinding by slaughtering random mobs just to gain a few levels.

When you take off the nostalgia glasses and look back at classic JRPGs, many of them have glaring problems, ranging from poorly balanced combat to mechanics that simply do not work as intended. Chained Echoes aims to be a classic 16-bit JRPG in its own right, but despite being developed by a single person, it benefits from decades of progress in game design to deliver an experience without any of those shortcomings.

Chained Echoes' experience is strongest in its complex combat system. It's unique, well thought-out and surprisingly well-balanced. It throws you into a wide variety of situations you'll have to puzzle-solve your way out of using the large selection of tools it gives you. This is not a game where you can press attack and win, or grind until you're overpowered. [h3]In my opinion, this is far better than any modern JRPG from Sega or Square Enix, and one of the best JRPGs. It overshadows big-budget titles from major JRPGs companies, despite being a solo passion project.[/h3]

[h1]Pros[/h1]

[h3] No Time-Wasting Filler Encounters[/h3] 
Modern JRPGs often pad the world with endless filler encounters. Chained Echoes respects your time by [b][u]eliminating random encounters entirely and drastically reducing mandatory battles.[/u][/b] Almost every fight is thoughtfully designed. For the first time, I genuinely enjoyed non-boss battles in a JRPG.

[h3] Combat That Finally Evolves[/h3]

Honestly, I was excited to play this at first. It makes a lot of improvements on the usual JRPG formula, modernizing it by getting rid of grinding and by streamlining the leveling process.

The dialogue is competently written, but the story got progressively more and more tedious with no interesting developments jumping out at me. I kinda stopped playing about an hour or so into Act 3 because there's honestly just nothing to motivate me continuing.

I played on the the hardest settings, but the Sky Armor sections become stat checks on this setting because you have to explore around for gear upgrades and I really don't want to bother with that. The normal combat is far more compelling and fun and I wish we could have just skipped the Sky Armors altogether.

Overall it's a disappointment. Half of the combat system (without the Sky Armors) is decent, while the story is boring. Did not finis

Overdrive system is stupid. Being hit sets you into overheat constantly and then you have to use skills that don’t help you as much to cool it down. 
Oh you need to heal after being hit? Too bad, it will cause you to be overheated and take double damage. 
There are lots of enemies with double attacks as well, causing you to be overheated for most of the battles without choice.
Not being able to level up and choose new skills without story checkpoints just makes this boring in between main story events. After 3 hours I was still not able to level up skills.

Wish I could refund the game at this point.
